_comment: The hand-picked section. This file is edited by a human; everything else in data/ is generated. Picked for evidence, not popularity: an entry earns a place here by reporting what it measured.

picks.why: The clearest measured win in the whole index: 261 IRS tax pages, 100% strict accuracy, ~$0.001 a page, 34× cheaper and 6× faster than the LLM pipeline it replaced.
The clearest measured loss, and it belongs here for the same reason: a futures bot ran on Jev decisions for 24 hours and finished 3.15% down over ~731 simulated trades.
Shows the pattern most projects converge on: Jev picks the action behind a confidence gate, and a writing model is kept in reserve for the parts that need prose.
The open answer to “do I need the API at all” — a 421M ModernBERT encoder with a typed decision head, RLCD training, published benchmarks and a ~35 ms forward pass.
A second, independent take on the same question: 395M parameters, 1-2 GB of CPU memory, 25-300 ms, and a claim to beat Jev on benchmarks that nobody has replicated yet.
Routing as a product rather than a demo: picks Codex's model, reasoning depth and speed mode on every single turn.
The most rigorous engineering in the index — context compaction with fallbacks, metrics, a shadow comparison against the old path, and a dashboard to watch it.
Jev as an alignment monitor, graded across four harmful-prompt benchmarks, reporting both better results and lower cost than the alternatives tested.
Someone actually checked the headline numbers instead of repeating them, and separates the claims that hold up from the ones that do not.
A whole search stack — query interpretation, source selection, relevance ranking — running on typed decisions at the edge.
